observation.visible_scene: A dark, dense storm-cloud field fills the frame throughout the excerpt. The clouds are mostly deep gray-blue with billowing, irregular textures. A faint brighter edge is visible near the lower-left corner in many frames, while the central and right portions remain dark except during intermittent internal brightening. No ground, horizon, rain, lightning channel, or other object is visible.
visible_changes: The scene is not uniformly dark: several diffuse brightening events occur within the cloud mass.
Around t=0.16-0.24 s, a bright glow appears in the lower-center/right area, illuminating surrounding cloud edges, then fades back to dark by t=0.32 s.
At t=0.80 s, another brief brightening appears in the lower-center region, then fades over the next few frames.
Around t=1.68-1.84 s, the lower-center clouds brighten again, producing a localized glow that fades by t=1.92 s.
From t=2.16 s to about t=2.64 s, a larger and brighter illuminated region develops across the central clouds, with strong light spreading around dark cloud silhouettes before fading by t=2.72 s.
Near t=3.04 s, a weaker brightening appears in the lower-center/left area, then fades toward the end of the clip.
Between these brightening intervals, the cloud texture and overall layout remain largely stable, with no obvious large-scale translation or deformation.
The brightening appears diffuse and internal to the clouds rather than a visible bolt crossing the frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the brightening is not directly visible; it may be intracloud lightning, sheet lightning, or another illumination source, but the excerpt does not show a channel or flash origin.
Whether the storm continues before or after this cropped segment is unknown.
The full duration and peak intensity of each brightening event may extend outside the sampled boundaries.
Any cloud motion outside this short excerpt, including drift direction or speed, cannot be determined.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is uncertain; the cloud layout appears mostly fixed relative to the frame, but subtle slow drift or very small camera movement cannot be ruled out.
It is unclear whether the brightening events are separate flashes or different stages of a continuing illumination process.
The exact shape and boundaries of the illuminated cloud regions are partly obscured by the dark foreground cloud masses.
No clear physical contact, onset, completion, or disappearance is supported; the clip begins and ends within an ongoing sequence of dark cloud illumination.
